chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who dies and has no wealth, and he said: 'He has one-third of his wealth, and the wife also [has one-third].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a deceased person who has no money or property to leave as a bequest?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a deceased person with minimal or no estate, affirming their right to bequeath one-third. The phrase 'and for the wife also' indicates that the wife’s share of the one-third bequest is distinct or that she is included in the beneficiaries of this specific bequest right, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the flexibility of the *thuluth* (one-third) limit for non-heirs or specific bequests even in modest estates. This highlights the practical application of the Prophet’s tradition that 'one-third is a large amount' for bequests, ensuring financial provisions are not lost due to lack of substantial wealth.
